bill.name: Drain the Intelligence Community Swamp Act of 2025 (H.R. 80)
bill.status: Introduced in House · Biggs / Davidson · referred to Oversight and Government Reform, Judiciary, and Armed Services on 2025-01-03
bill.analyzed: All substantive provisions in the introduced bill (4 pages; §§1–2), with the sole substantive provision in §2.

sourceLimits: The supplied raw file contains all substantive provisions of the introduced bill as flattened one-line text but no metadata sidecar, page boundaries, current person-level clearance data, investigation baseline, implementation records, or public-reporting requirement; it also omits the standard enacting clause visible in the official PDF. The official Congress.gov PDF establishes the four-page count; no outside facts are used to infer who currently holds a clearance, whether any related investigation already exists, or whether either action would become public. The statement-signatory description and the terms “Hunter Biden laptop scandal,” “role,” and “level of engagement” are the bill’s characterizations and investigation subjects, not findings established by this source. The bill states no measurable downstream outcome. No defensible recurring official series or empirical conditional follows, so metrics and conditionals are empty and no series hints or stance matrices are supplied.

provisions.title: Section 2 — Revocation of security clearances
provisions.heading: §2: Clearance revocation and future bar; investigations of 51 named individuals
provisions.quote: “Not later than 24 hours after the date of enactment of this Act, the security clearance of any individual listed in subsection (c), signatories of the statement titled Public Statement on the Hunter Biden Emails dated October 19, 2020, are hereby revoked, and no security clearance may be granted or renewed for any such individual.” … “The Secretary of Defense and the Attorney General shall investigate such individuals and their role in the Hunter Biden laptop scandal and level of engagement with the Biden Presidential campaign.”
provisions.context: Section 2 is the bill’s only substantive section. Subsection (a) directs that, no later than 24 hours after enactment, any security clearance of an individual named in subsection (c) be revoked and prohibits any later grant or renewal for that individual. Subsection (b) directs the Secretary of Defense and Attorney General to investigate the same people. Subsection (c) supplies a fixed list of 51 names; subsection (a) describes the listed individuals as signatories of the October 19, 2020 statement identified there. The 24-hour deadline modifies the clearance revocation, not the investigations. The text does not define “security clearance,” identify the official responsible for carrying out or recording the revocations, set an investigation deadline or division of responsibility, require findings or a report, or direct public disclosure.
goals: Revoke within 24 hours of enactment any security clearance held by each of the 51 named individuals and bar any later grant or renewal for those individuals.

Require the Secretary of Defense and the Attorney General to investigate the named individuals’ role in the bill-described “Hunter Biden laptop scandal” and their level of engagement with the Biden Presidential campaign.

effects.text: If enacted, any existing security clearance held by a listed individual would be statutorily revoked within 24 hours, but the number of people practically affected cannot be derived from the text because it does not say which, if any, currently holds an active clearance.
The bill would prohibit granting or renewing a security clearance for any listed individual and states no sunset, waiver, exception, or reinstatement mechanism.

effects.mechanism: Mandatory investigations without a specified endpoint
effects.text: The Secretary of Defense and the Attorney General would be required to investigate the listed individuals on the stated subjects, but the mandate does not itself establish wrongdoing and requires no particular finding, charge, report, publication, or other consequence.

barriers.text: Subsection (a) uses a self-executing passive construction without naming an executing official or coordinating agency, while compliance would require locating any relevant clearance records and carrying the prohibition into later grant and renewal decisions.

The list supplies names without unique identifiers, and the 24-hour revocation deadline leaves little time to match those names, confirm any current clearance status, and communicate any required revocation.

barriers.actor: Secretary of Defense and Attorney General
barriers.text: The investigation subjects use undefined terms, and beyond naming those subjects, the bill gives the two officials no deadline, division of responsibility, procedures, evidentiary standard, deliverable, or completion rule.

The bill creates no reporting or publication requirement, and the supplied source contains neither person-level clearance status nor investigation records, so external observers could not determine complete implementation from the bill text or a named official data product.
